title: Plant Parts We Eat: Parent Guide
endLine: Every plant food comes from a plant part with a job.

scenes.tts: Which part of a plant is a carrot? And what does that part do? A bag of groceries and one big drawing let your child find out.
scenes.caption: Which part of a plant is a carrot? And what does that part do? A bag of groceries and one big drawing let your child find out.
scenes.visual: Warm schematic kitchen table seen from above. A large sheet of paper fills most of the frame, with a grocery bag tipped beside it: a carrot, broccoli and an apple peek out. Large high-contrast text: 'Which part is a carrot?' No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Which part of a plant is a carrot? And what does that part do? A bag of groceries and one big drawing let your child find out.

scenes.visual: Same table. The title 'Plant Parts We Eat' appears above the paper while the grocery bag settles.

scenes.tts: Fruits and vegetables come from plant parts. Each part had a job. Your child practices sorting, looking for clues, and changing a guess after checking it.
scenes.caption: Fruits and vegetables come from plant parts. Each part had a job. Your child practices sorting, looking for clues, and changing a guess after checking it.
scenes.visual: On the paper, a simple plant draws itself: roots below a soil line, a stem, leaves, a flower and a fruit with seeds. Three short labels appear beside it: 'Sort', 'Find clues', 'Change the guess'.
scenes.narration: Fruits and vegetables come from plant parts. Each part had a job. Your child practices sorting, looking for clues, and changing a guess after checking it.

scenes.tts: Check for food allergies first. Use pictures for foods your child needs to avoid. Gather paper, markers, a carrot, asparagus, lettuce, broccoli, an apple, and a tomato. Add canned beans or frozen peas, a firm potato without green skin or sprouts, and celery with leaves.
scenes.caption: Check for food allergies first. Use pictures for foods your child needs to avoid. Gather paper, markers, a carrot, asparagus, lettuce, broccoli, an apple, and a tomato. Add canned beans or frozen peas, a firm potato without green skin or sprouts, and celery with leaves.
scenes.visual: On the kitchen table, show an allergy check before the groceries come out. Then show paper, markers and the listed foods in small groups. Show a photo card standing in for an ingredient the child needs to avoid.
scenes.narration: Check for food allergies first. Use pictures for foods your child needs to avoid. Gather paper, markers, a carrot, asparagus, lettuce, broccoli, an apple, and a tomato. Add canned beans or frozen peas, a firm potato without green skin or sprouts, and celery with leaves.

scenes.tts: Help your child draw the plant and label each part. Wash the produce. You cut the apple and the tomato across the middle, so the seeds show. Leave everything else whole.
scenes.caption: Help your child draw the plant and label each part. Wash the produce. You cut the apple and the tomato across the middle, so the seeds show. Leave everything else whole.
scenes.visual: The plant drawing gains labels one by one: 'root', 'stem', 'leaf', 'flower', 'fruit', 'seeds'. On a cutting board, an adult hand cuts the apple and tomato across the middle, showing the seeds inside.
scenes.narration: Help your child draw the plant and label each part. Wash the produce. You cut the apple and the tomato across the middle, so the seeds show. Leave everything else whole.

scenes.tts: Hold up one food at a time. Ask, 'Which part of the plant do you think this is?' Let your child place it on the drawing. Don't correct anything yet. That first sort is the guess.
scenes.caption: Hold up one food at a time. Ask, 'Which part of the plant do you think this is?' Let your child place it on the drawing. Don't correct anything yet. That first sort is the guess.
scenes.visual: A drawn adult hand holds up the broccoli; a speech bubble asks 'Which part?' A child's hand places foods on the drawing; the broccoli lands by the leaves, the carrot by the roots, and the potato by the roots too.
scenes.narration: Hold up one food at a time. Ask, 'Which part of the plant do you think this is?' Let your child place it on the drawing. Don't correct anything yet. That first sort is the guess.

scenes.tts: Now go back and look for clues. A tomato grows from a flower and holds seeds, so it is a fruit. Look for thin side roots on the carrot or marks where they were trimmed. Ask, 'What is your clue?'
scenes.caption: Now go back and look for clues. A tomato grows from a flower and holds seeds, so it is a fruit. Look for thin side roots on the carrot or marks where they were trimmed. Ask, 'What is your clue?'
scenes.visual: Highlight the seeds in the cut tomato and move it to the fruit. Show thin side roots or trim marks on the carrot, and keep it at the roots. Let the child's hand move food when a clue changes the guess.
scenes.narration: Now go back and look for clues. A tomato grows from a flower and holds seeds, so it is a fruit. Look for thin side roots on the carrot or marks where they were trimmed. Ask, 'What is your clue?'

scenes.tts: Here is one for you. Look closely at a head of broccoli. Which part of the plant are you holding?
scenes.caption: Here is one for you. Look closely at a head of broccoli. Which part of the plant are you holding?
scenes.visual: A large drawn head of broccoli fills the right side. A high-contrast question card on the left reads: 'Broccoli: which plant part?'
scenes.narration: Here is one for you. Look closely at a head of broccoli. Which part of the plant are you holding?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and the broccoli. Subtle ambient motion: the broccoli bumps catch a soft moving light, nothing revealed.

scenes.tts: Each small green bump is a flower bud. Left to grow, the buds open into small yellow flowers. So broccoli moves to the flower.
scenes.caption: Each small green bump is a flower bud. Left to grow, the buds open into small yellow flowers. So broccoli moves to the flower.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the broccoli: each bump is ringed as a bud. A short time-lapse shows a few buds opening into small yellow flowers. The broccoli then slides across the drawing to the flower. Label: 'Flower buds'.
scenes.narration: Each small green bump is a flower bud. Left to grow, the buds open into small yellow flowers. So broccoli moves to the flower.

scenes.tts: Now check the trick cards. Look at the potato's eyes with your child. Each eye is a bud, like a bud on a stem. A potato is an underground stem. Celery is mostly long leaf stalks. Look for the leaves at the top.
scenes.caption: Now check the trick cards. Look at the potato's eyes with your child. Each eye is a bud, like a bud on a stem. A potato is an underground stem. Celery is mostly long leaf stalks. Look for the leaves at the top.
scenes.visual: The potato sits beside a drawn twig with buds; matching rings link the potato's eyes to the twig's buds. Label: 'Underground stem'. The potato slides from the roots to the stem. Then the celery stalk shows its leaves at the top and slides to the leaves.
scenes.narration: Now check the trick cards. Look at the potato's eyes with your child. Each eye is a bud, like a bud on a stem. A potato is an underground stem. Celery is mostly long leaf stalks. Look for the leaves at the top.

scenes.tts: Point to each part and ask what it does. Roots take in water. Stems hold the plant up. Leaves make food using light. Flowers make seeds, and the fruit holds them.
scenes.caption: Point to each part and ask what it does. Roots take in water. Stems hold the plant up. Leaves make food using light. Flowers make seeds, and the fruit holds them.
scenes.visual: The finished drawing with every food in place. Each part glows in turn with a one- or two-word job label: 'Water in', 'Holds up', 'Makes food', 'Makes seeds', 'Holds seeds'.
scenes.narration: Point to each part and ask what it does. Roots take in water. Stems hold the plant up. Leaves make food using light. Flowers make seeds, and the fruit holds them.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child the whole time food is out. You do all the cutting and put the knife away. Tasting is optional. Check allergies first, and cut small pieces onto a clean plate. Never taste raw potato. Wash your hands and have your child wash theirs when you finish.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child the whole time food is out. You do all the cutting and put the knife away. Tasting is optional. Check allergies first, and cut small pieces onto a clean plate. Never taste raw potato. Wash your hands and have your child wash theirs when you finish.
scenes.visual: At the table, show the adult beside the child, putting the knife away. Show a 'Sort only' label by the plant drawing and a crossed-out raw potato slice. Then show the adult and child washing their hands at the sink.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child the whole time food is out. You do all the cutting and put the knife away. Tasting is optional. Check allergies first, and cut small pieces onto a clean plate. Never taste raw potato. Wash your hands and have your child wash theirs when you finish.

scenes.tts: Keep small food pieces away from children under four. Whole peas, beans, and hard chunks of raw carrot or apple are choking hazards. Call nine one one if a child is choking.
scenes.caption: Keep small food pieces away from children under four. Whole peas, beans, and hard chunks of raw carrot or apple are choking hazards. Call nine one one if a child is choking.
scenes.visual: Show whole peas, beans, and hard chunks of raw carrot and apple next to the label 'Under 4: choking risk'. Replace the examples with a phone icon and the label 'Choking: call 911'.
scenes.narration: Keep small food pieces away from children under four. Whole peas, beans, and hard chunks of raw carrot or apple are choking hazards. Call nine one one if a child is choking.

scenes.tts: End by asking, 'Which part of the plant is a carrot, and what does that part do?' If your child is unsure, go back to the drawing and check the carrot together. The root holds the plant in the ground and takes in water.
scenes.caption: End by asking, 'Which part of the plant is a carrot, and what does that part do?' If your child is unsure, go back to the drawing and check the carrot together. The root holds the plant in the ground and takes in water.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the sorting drawing. Bring the carrot forward and highlight its place below the soil line. Show the root holding the plant and taking in water.
scenes.narration: End by asking, 'Which part of the plant is a carrot, and what does that part do?' If your child is unsure, go back to the drawing and check the carrot together. The root holds the plant in the ground and takes in water.

scenes.line: Every plant food comes from a plant part with a job.
scenes.visual: Clean warm end card with a faint plant drawing in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'Every plant food comes from a plant part with a job.'
